newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power seen up on San Onofre 2 nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power seen up on San Onofre 2 nuke outage.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher on the weekend outage of the San Onofre 2 nuclear power unit, market sources said.

In over-the-counter business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $33.00-33.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) higher than Friday's settlement at $32.26 and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $20.25-20.50 versus Friday's close at $22.37.
Southern California Edison Co decided to shut 1,070 megawatt(MW) San Onofre 2 Sunday to replace its charge line check valves after already scaling output back to 90 percent last Thursday.
The valve work could continue into the end of the week, market sources said.
San Onofre 3, rated at 1,080 MW, remained in cold shutdown after being taken offline April 12 for refueling and was scheduled to resume operation around July 10.
The latest six to 10 day forecasts showed temperatures in the Pacific Northwest would average below normal, while those in the Southwest would run above normal.

The WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state continued to await clearance from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission before beginning start-up operations, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday, adding the unit would be "physically ready" to resume operations by late tonight or early Friday.

Several Western coal-fired power units were set to return to the power grid by this week, including a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., a 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado.
Late Friday, the Western Systems Coordinating Council board approved a derating of the Pacific Intertie transmission sytem to 6,300 MW from the current 7,200 MW, which was effective Saturday.
